entry.title: Dynamic Top-N Waterfall Analysis in SAP Analytics Cloud: Why I Moved Ranking to SAP Datasphere
entry.content:
Dynamic Top-N Waterfall Analysis in SAP Analytics Cloud: Why I Moved Ranking to SAP Datasphere

Introduction

Waterfall charts are useful for explaining how individual business drivers contribute to the movement between two values. In enterprise planning and reporting, however, the requirement often goes beyond displaying a static set of drivers.

In one of my implementations, the business requirement was to dynamically display:

Top 6 Drivers + All Others

The ranking needed to respond to the user's current analytical context, including selections such as Region, Business Unit, Country, Product Group, Period, Version, and Reporting Frequency.

Initially, I considered performing the ranking in SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC). As the requirement developed, I found that performing this type of dynamic ranking in SAC introduced additional processing and scripting complexity.

I therefore changed the architecture so that the analytical context is passed from SAC to SAP Datasphere through input parameters. Datasphere performs the aggregation, variance calculation, ranking, and All Others calculation, while SAC consumes a small visualization-ready result.

This article explains that design pattern, the reasoning behind it, and when I would consider using this approach instead of SAC-side ranking.

1. Business Requirement

 

Consider a comparison between two planning versions:

Version A vs. Version B

For each business driver, the variance is calculated as:

VARIANCE_AMOUNT =
    VERSION_A_AMOUNT - VERSION_B_AMOUNT

The business does not want to display every driver in the waterfall.

Instead, the requirement is to show the six drivers with the largest absolute impact, followed by one residual category:

Driver Rank 1
Driver Rank 2
Driver Rank 3
Driver Rank 4
Driver Rank 5
Driver Rank 6
All Others

Therefore, regardless of how many detailed drivers exist in the underlying dataset, SAC ultimately needs only seven driver rows for the waterfall.

The important complication is that these seven rows are not static.

If the user changes Region, Business Unit, Country, Product Group, Period, Version, or Frequency, the Top 6 can change completely.

2. My Initial Approach: Ranking in SAC

 

My first consideration was to perform the ranking in SAC.

The application would determine the Top 6 drivers and dynamically update the corresponding waterfall labels.

Conceptually:

Detailed Dataset
      ↓
     SAC
      ↓
Apply User Filters
      ↓
Calculate Variance
      ↓
Determine Top 6
      ↓
Calculate All Others
      ↓
Update Dynamic Labels
      ↓
Waterfall

This can work well for simpler requirements.

The challenge in my case was that SAC needed access to the broader driver population before determining which six records belonged in the Top 6.

Every important filter change could require the application logic to determine the ranking again, calculate the residual All Others amount, and update the dynamic driver labels.

As more business dimensions, versions, and reporting frequencies were introduced, the SAC-side implementation became increasingly complex.

The question I eventually asked was:

Why bring the larger driver population into the visualization layer when the data layer can determine the final seven rows first?

That changed the architecture.

3. Moving the Ranking to SAP Datasphere

 

Instead of treating ranking primarily as visualization logic, I moved it into the analytical data layer.

The runtime flow became:

SAC User Selections
        ↓
Datasphere Input Parameters
        ↓
Apply Analytical Context
        ↓
Aggregate Version A / Version B
        ↓
Calculate Variance
        ↓
Rank Drivers
        ↓
Top 6
        ↓
Calculate All Others
        ↓
Return 7 Rows
        ↓
SAC Waterfall

SAC remains responsible for the user experience and visualization.

Datasphere becomes responsible for preparing the analytical result required by that experience.

This separation simplified the implementation and reduced the amount of ranking-related processing required in the SAC application.

4. Passing the Analytical Context

 

Passing SAC Selections as Input Parameters

The Top-N result must reflect the user's current analytical context.

For example, the application might provide selections for:

Region
Business Unit
Country
Product Group
Period
Version
Frequency

These selections are passed to Datasphere through input parameters.

Datasphere can then apply the selected context before performing the aggregation and ranking logic.

This is important because the objective is not to calculate one universal Top 6 list. The objective is to calculate the Top 6 that is relevant to the user's current selection.

Why Ranking Must Follow the Selected Context

A driver's rank is not necessarily a permanent characteristic of that driver.

For example, the same driver could be:

Rank 1 for Region A
Rank 8 for Region B
Rank 3 for Business Unit A
Outside Top 6 for Business Unit B

The ranking can also change when the user selects another period, version, product group, or reporting frequency.

For this reason, I treat rank as a context-dependent analytical result rather than a fixed master-data attribute.

The analytical context must first be established, and the ranking should then be calculated within that context.

5. Aggregate Before Ranking

 

Aggregation at Driver Level

Another important design decision is the sequence of operations.

I first aggregate the measures to the required driver level.

A simplified example is:

SELECT
    DRIVER,
    SUM(VERSION_A_AMOUNT) AS VERSION_A_AMOUNT,
    SUM(VERSION_B_AMOUNT) AS VERSION_B_AMOUNT
FROM ...
GROUP BY DRIVER

This creates one analytical result for each driver within the selected context.

Calculate Variance After Aggregation

Once Version A and Version B have been aggregated to the appropriate level, the variance can be calculated:

VERSION_A_AMOUNT - VERSION_B_AMOUNT
    AS VARIANCE_AMOUNT

Only after this aggregation and variance calculation should the ranking be performed.

The processing sequence is therefore:

FILTER
  ↓
AGGREGATE
  ↓
CALCULATE VARIANCE
  ↓
RANK
  ↓
TOP 6
  ↓
ALL OTHERS

This sequence is important because ranking detailed records before they have been aggregated to the required analytical level can produce a different result.

6. Ranking the Drivers

 

For my requirement, I used a window-function pattern based on ROW_NUMBER().

A simplified example is:

ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY <analytical context>
    ORDER BY ABS(VARIANCE_AMOUNT) DESC
) AS DRIVER_RANK

The exact partitioning depends on the analytical grain and modeling requirements.

The important part of the ranking is:

ORDER BY ABS(VARIANCE_AMOUNT) DESC

I rank by the absolute value of the variance because both positive and negative drivers can be significant.

For example:

Driver A     +12.0
Driver B      -9.5
Driver C      +8.0

Driver B should not disappear simply because its variance is negative.

Its magnitude is 9.5, so it represents a larger movement than Driver C.

However, ABS() is used only to determine the ranking order. The original signed variance is retained for the waterfall so that the visualization continues to distinguish positive and negative contributions.

7. Selecting the Top 6

 

Once the ranking is available, selecting the six largest drivers is straightforward:

WHERE DRIVER_RANK <= 6

This produces:

Rank 1
Rank 2
Rank 3
Rank 4
Rank 5
Rank 6

At this point, however, the waterfall does not necessarily reconcile to the complete variance because the remaining drivers have not yet been represented.

That is where All Others becomes important.

8. Calculating All Others

 

In my implementation, I calculate All Others as a residual rather than returning every lower-ranked driver to SAC.

The logic is:

All Others =
    Total Variance
    -
    Sum of Top 6 Variance

Conceptually:

ALL_OTHERS_AMOUNT =
    TOTAL_VARIANCE - TOP6_VARIANCE

For example:

Total Variance        45.0
Top 6 Variance        65.0
--------------------------
All Others           -20.0

The final dataset returned to the visualization could therefore look like:

Driver A         +15.0
Driver B         +14.0
Driver C         +12.0
Driver D         +10.0
Driver E          +8.0
Driver F          +6.0
All Others       -20.0
-----------------------
Total             45.0

The waterfall can now reconcile to the overall variance while remaining compact.

Instead of transferring every individual driver to SAC solely for ranking and consolidation, the analytical layer returns the records needed by the visualization.

9. Final Architecture

 

Figure 1: Dynamic Top-N waterfall architecture using SAP Analytics Cloud and SAP Datasphere

[KEEP YOUR EXISTING FIGURE 1 HERE]

The architecture can be summarized as:

SAC User Selections
        ↓
Input Parameters
        ↓
Datasphere Filter Context
        ↓
Aggregate Version A / Version B
        ↓
Calculate Variance
        ↓
Rank by ABS(Variance)
        ↓
Top 6
        ↓
All Others = Total - Sum(Top 6)
        ↓
7 Visualization-Ready Rows
        ↓
SAC Waterfall

The important point is that SAC does not need to determine the Top 6 from the complete driver population.

SAC provides the analytical selections.

Datasphere performs the context filtering, aggregation, variance calculation, ranking, and residual calculation and returns the result required by the waterfall.

10. What Changed After Moving the Logic

 

Faster Response

One benefit I observed was that SAC no longer needed to handle the broader driver population specifically for determining the Top 6 and All Others.

The data-intensive processing was performed before the final visualization-ready result was consumed by SAC.

Instead of using the visualization layer to discover the Top 6 from a broader dataset, the application receives the reduced result required for presentation.

Less SAC Scripting

This was equally important for my implementation.

With the initial approach, SAC application logic needed to manage ranking-related processing, residual calculations, and dynamic driver labels.

After moving the analytical logic upstream, the SAC responsibility became closer to:

Capture Selections
        ↓
Pass Input Parameters
        ↓
Refresh Data
        ↓
Display Waterfall

Reducing the amount of application scripting also made the solution easier for me to understand, troubleshoot, and maintain.

11. Extending the Pattern Beyond Top 6

 

Top 6 was the business requirement for this particular waterfall.

It is not a technical limitation of the architecture.

In another waterfall requirement, I needed a pattern such as:

Top 6
+
Bottom 3
+
All Others

The same general architecture can support that requirement by changing the ranking and classification logic in the analytical layer.

Other requirements could include:

Top 5 + All Others

Top 10 + All Others

Top 5 + Bottom 5 + All Others

without fundamentally redesigning the SAC application.

This is one reason I prefer treating more complex Top-N selection as an analytical-modeling concern rather than hard-coding a particular number of drivers into visualization logic.

12. When Should Ranking Move to Datasphere?

 

This pattern does not mean that every Top-N requirement should automatically be implemented in Datasphere.

There are situations where SAC-side ranking is entirely appropriate.

When SAC-Side Ranking May Be Sufficient

I would consider keeping the ranking in SAC when:

  • The dataset is relatively small.
  • The Top-N requirement is straightforward.
  • Only a limited number of filter contexts need to be supported.
  • Dynamic residual calculations such as All Others are simple.
  • SAC scripting remains limited and easy to maintain.
  • Moving the calculation upstream would introduce unnecessary modeling complexity.

For those scenarios, adding another Datasphere model simply to calculate a small Top-N result may not provide enough benefit.

When Datasphere-Side Ranking Becomes More Useful

I would consider moving the ranking to Datasphere when:

  • The broader driver population is large.
  • Ranking must dynamically respond to several business dimensions.
  • Multiple versions, periods, and reporting frequencies are involved.
  • Top-N and All Others must be recalculated for many filter combinations.
  • The same ranking pattern needs to be reused by multiple analytical experiences.
  • SAC application scripting starts becoming difficult to maintain.
  • Only a small visualization-ready result is ultimately required by SAC.

The decision therefore depends on the data volume, analytical complexity, reuse requirements, and responsibilities of each layer.

My goal is not to move calculations upstream simply because Datasphere can perform them. The goal is to place the calculation where it can be executed and maintained most effectively.

Conclusion

 

A Top-N waterfall can initially appear to be only a visualization requirement.

Once the ranking must dynamically respond to multiple business dimensions, versions, periods, and reporting frequencies, however, it can become an analytical architecture problem.

In my implementation, moving the ranking from SAC to SAP Datasphere resulted in a clearer division of responsibilities:

SAP Datasphere

Filter → Aggregate → Calculate → Rank → Consolidate

SAP Analytics Cloud

Select → Refresh → Visualize → Interact

For this dynamic Top-N driver-analysis requirement, the approach gave me a smaller visualization-ready result, faster response, and substantially less SAC scripting.

At the same time, I would not use this pattern for every Top-N visualization. For a smaller dataset, a straightforward ranking requirement, and a limited number of filter combinations, SAC-side ranking can be sufficient and keeps the architecture simple. When the ranking must operate over a broader dataset and repeatedly adapt across multiple dimensions, versions, periods, and frequencies, I prefer to let Datasphere prepare the final analytical result and let SAC focus on interaction and presentation.

entry.title: User Insights: SAP Business Data Cloud practitioners’ recommendations for BW modernization
entry.content:
For many data professionals responsible for SAP BW, the modernization challenge begins with a difficult question: how do you move forward without discarding the business knowledge embedded in the system?

A mature BW environment is more than a collection of tables. It may contain years of transformations, hierarchies, security rules, custom CompositeProviders, DataStore Objects, InfoCubes, and queries. These assets often encode business definitions that users depend on, even when those definitions are not documented elsewhere. At the same time, maintaining the existing environment can consume resources that organizations would rather direct toward cloud analytics, data products, and AI.

These competing priorities define the BW Modernizer.

This is the second article in a series examining four SAP Business Data Cloud practitioner profiles identified through user stories on the PeerSpot peer-to-peer platform. Our first article explored the FP&A Modernizer, focusing on the journey from fragmented financial data and manual reporting processes to insight that people can understand, trust, and act on. This article turns to a different practitioner reality: teams that already have a mature analytical foundation in BW, but need to modernize it without losing the business meaning that makes it valuable. The BW Modernizer has a different starting point. The organization already possesses a substantial analytical foundation. Its challenge is to preserve the value of that foundation while progressively adopting a modern architecture.

When technical debt and business value occupy the same system

A typical BW Modernizer operates BW 7.x, BW on HANA, or BW/4HANA, with SAP ECC or SAP S/4HANA among its source systems. The environment may support SAP Analytics Cloud, SAP BusinessObjects, or other reporting tools and contain significant custom development accumulated over many years. This creates a tension familiar to many experienced practitioners. Existing BW models contain valuable context and proven logic. Yet reproducing every historical object in a new platform can transform modernization into an expensive technical conversion exercise. Conversely, replacing the environment without understanding its semantics risks losing definitions, dependencies, and controls that the business still needs.

Practitioners are therefore looking for a path that protects continuity without preserving every legacy design decision indefinitely. They want to move at a manageable pace, identify what should be retained, and make existing BW data available for new analytics and AI use cases while modernization continues. The core modernization task is therefore not to migrate BW object by object. It is to separate durable business meaning from legacy implementation detail, then rebuild the most valuable knowledge as governed, reusable data products and semantic assets.

Practitioner insight 1: Begin with fit analysis, not migration code

Arindam Das, Director and Architect at Innoverv, describes a structured approach for moving BW and BW/4HANA workloads toward BDC. The first step is to map existing InfoCubes against standard BDC data products. Practitioners then identify functional gaps and decide whether those gaps require an extension to a standard product or the creation of a custom data product in SAP Datasphere.

  • “From BW InfoCubes, we need to convert them into data products, starting with mapping the BW InfoCubes with the standard data product. If mapping is not possible, we have to build custom data products to fill any gaps. The first step is conducting a fit analysis with existing BW models, identifying gaps, and developing the custom data products on the Datasphere layer.”
  • Arindam Das, Director and Architect, Innoverv

This changes the central question from “How do we convert every BW object?” to “Which business capabilities already have an appropriate target, and where is custom logic still justified?” That distinction helps prevent migration from reproducing unnecessary complexity. Standard data products become the baseline, and custom development is reserved for gaps with a clear business purpose.

Read PeerSpot review

Once teams know which capabilities deserve a place in the target architecture, the next challenge is deciding what exactly must be carried forward.

Practitioner insight 2: Preserve meaning, not every implementation detail

A BW modernization program must distinguish valuable business semantics from legacy technical structures. A hierarchy, currency conversion, authorization rule, or calculation may still be essential, even if the object or pipeline implementing it is not. Santosh Pallai, Solutions Architect at NTT DATA, describes an architecture in which SAP Datasphere contains dimensions, fact tables, relationships, calculations, hierarchies, and business rules. Reusable analytical data products sit above this semantic foundation, while SAP Analytics Cloud remains focused on planning, analysis, and visualization.

  • “Once business logic, calculations, hierarchies, and currency conversions are modeled in Datasphere, I can reuse the same analytical models across multiple reports, dashboards, and planning stories. This improves consistency, reduces duplication of effort, enhances performance, and simplifies long-term maintenance.”
  • Santosh Pallai, Solutions Architect, NTT DATA

For the BW Modernizer, semantic preservation should be a deliberate architecture responsibility. Business logic should be identified, validated, and positioned in the target semantic layer rather than scattered across recreated reports. A useful test for each legacy object is whether it contains reusable business meaning or simply reflects how data had to be processed in the previous architecture.

Read PeerSpot review

With reusable meaning defined, modernization can start creating value before the entire BW estate has been redesigned.

Practitioner insight 3: Use data products to create value before modernization is complete

Large BW estates rarely modernize in a single step. Data products provide a way to expose valuable BW data while the broader transformation continues. SAP’s published reference architecture describes BW as a data producer, with the Data Product Generator making BW data available as customer-managed data products in BDC for use in Datasphere, Analytics Cloud, and SAP Databricks scenarios. Arindam Das’ approach uses standard data products as the baseline, with selective extensions for fields or requirements not covered by the standard model. In his architecture, Datasphere provides the semantic layer, Databricks supports AI and machine learning, and Analytics Cloud delivers presentation. This makes modernization incremental. Teams can expose high-value datasets first, validate consumption patterns, and use what they learn to prioritize the next wave of work.

  • If standard data products do not fit the needs, we try to extend them where possible. For instance, the customer master is a standard data product, but it does not always include all necessary fields. If certain custom fields exist in the customer data product in BW, we extend the standard products accordingly. If a required data product is not available from SAP, we build a new data product using ABAP.
  • Arindam Das, Director and Architect, Innoverv

As reusable data products begin to emerge, standardization becomes a business discipline rather than a purely technical preference.

Practitioner insight 4: Make standardization part of the business case

Technical teams often evaluate modernization options in terms of infrastructure cost, migration effort, or individual platform features. PeerSpot practitioners also emphasize the operational value of standardization. Sweety Khandelwal, Principal Consultant at Mercedes-Benz AG, describes the modernization of a global HR analytics environment from BW on HANA to BDC. Her account highlights the challenges of supporting worldwide HR processes and the difficulty of managing extensive customization at enterprise scale.

  • “For HR-related processes, managing HR-related activities for the entire world brings a lot of customization, and if we go ahead with tools that require high customization and minimal standardization, it becomes difficult for an organization as large as Mercedes to standardize it. For better standardization and to easily use other SAP source systems, SAP Business Data Cloud was the best option we could select.”
  • Sweety Khandelwal, Principal Consultant, Mercedes-Benz AG

The value case is not just infrastructure migration. Standardization can reduce independently maintained definitions and custom solutions across regions, business units, or functional teams. The goal is not to eliminate necessary differentiation, but to make customization an explicit decision rather than the default response to every requirement.

Read PeerSpot review

That discipline also creates a cleaner foundation for the more advanced analytics and AI scenarios that often justify modernization.

Practitioner insight 5: Modernize progressively toward analytics and AI

The BW Modernizer is usually motivated by more than platform lifecycle concerns. Practitioners want to make established enterprise data available for use cases that were difficult to implement in the legacy environment. Muhammad Ashar, SAP Data and Analytics Consultant at Dezert Innovation Technology Company, describes using SAP Databricks within BDC to develop and test machine-learning models with multiple datasets.

  • “In Databricks within SAP Business Data Cloud, we can write ML algorithms, train our models, have test cases available, bring in data sets, and have access to these capabilities. It provides so much freedom.”
  • Muhammad Ashar, SAP Data and Analytics Consultant, Dezert Innovation Technology Company

Although this implementation was greenfield rather than a BW migration, it illustrates the destination that can motivate modernization: SAP data combined with additional datasets, processed through ML/AI, and surfaced in analytical experiences.

Read PeerSpot review

For BW practitioners, AI should not be a disconnected workstream. Existing BW data may contain years of curated history and business context that can support forecasting, anomaly detection, and other machine-learning scenarios.

The modernization roadmap can therefore progress in deliberate stages:

  1. Stabilize and assess the existing BW estate.
  2. Map valuable BW assets to standard or custom data products.
  3. Preserve reusable logic in the semantic layer.
  4. Enable new analytics and data-product consumption.
  5. Extend selected datasets into AI and machine-learning scenarios.

These stages do not require a single, disruptive cutover. The key is to connect each decision to a target business or analytical outcome.

A practical checklist for the BW Modernizer

PeerSpot’s practitioner insights suggest several questions for teams shaping their roadmap:

  • Which BW models are still actively used, and which can be retired?
  • Which objects contain essential semantics, calculations, hierarchies, or security rules?
  • Which existing requirements align with standard data products?
  • Where is custom extension genuinely necessary?
  • Is reusable business logic being positioned in the semantic layer rather than duplicated in reports?
  • Can selected BW assets be made available as reusable data products before the wider transformation is complete?
  • Is standardization included in the value case alongside infrastructure and licensing?
  • Which trusted BW datasets could support new analytics, forecasting, anomaly detection, or AI use cases?

The goal is not to transfer technical debt into a new environment. It is to preserve valuable context while replacing structures that limit how the data can be used.

The broader lesson for data professionals

These practitioners point to a consistent principle: BW modernization should be an evolution of business context, not a replication of legacy architecture. Fit analysis shows what should move. Standard data products reduce unnecessary redevelopment. A governed semantic layer protects reusable business meaning. Incremental exposure creates value before the full journey is complete. Standardization keeps new customization debt under control.

For the BW Modernizer, success is not measured by the number of converted objects. It is measured by whether trusted enterprise data becomes easier to reuse, govern, explain, and apply to new decisions. The opportunity is not simply to relocate BW, but to turn its accumulated knowledge into a governed foundation for analytics, reusable data products, and AI-ready decision-making.

What we'll explore next 

In the next article in this series, we will examine the Business AI Builder, and the architecture decisions practitioners make when they can design a BDC environment for AI without legacy constraints.

entry.title: Ask your Questions: How Graphical Views in SAP Datasphere Support SAP Analytics Cloud
entry.content:
Dear data analysts and data architects,

Are you and your company working with SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC) for data analysis and want to use SAP Datasphere to create a harmonized, reliable, real-time-capable data fundament? Do you need an easy graphical tool to design it?

Then, we recommend the graphical view model type and analytical model in SAP Datasphere. Did you already start with first models and want to gain a deeper understanding? 
Which options exist to influence the SAP Datasphere graphical view performance ?
How a data access control can restrict data visibility for SAP Datasphere graphical view?
How SAC Seamless Planning interacts with SAP Datasphere?
How advance AI can be leveraged in SAP Business Data Cloud?

 

 Then, you should register to this live session:

Exploring SAP Datasphere Graphical View modeling options for SAP Analytics Cloud Stories

You can even ask your own questions.

For example, the following questions were asked in previous sessions:

Q: When sharing a view, do other users need a connection to the source?

A: No. Users can view the data directly, similar to SAP Analytics Cloud or third-party tools.

Q: Do we need separate connections for each space?

A:  SAC uses one live connection to connect to Datasphere.

In SAP datasphere, connections are created inside a space. You need to create a connection per space. Users only see spaces assigned to their roles.
However, Datasphere in SAP BDC uses a universal connection concept. When you use SAP BDC, you only need to define the source connections in SAP BDC and the system will create all necessary spaces in SAP datasphere when you install SAP BDC intelligent content.

Q: 

How does Datasphere security align with SAP security?

They are different but related:

SAP:

  • Transaction-based authorization
  • System-wide roles
  • Authorization based on object names and type of activity
  • Authorizations are grouped in Roles, standard role templates exist

SAC:

  • Activity-based roles exist
  • User groups exist
  • Authorization only per object or folder
  • standard role templates exist

SAP Datasphere:

  • Space-specific roles
  • No user groups exist
  • Authorization only per space, not per object name or folder
  • Standard role templates exist

Similarities:

  • Row-level authorization: Data Access Control (DAC) – like CDS access control
  • Roles give specific activities for specific types of objects and need to be assigned to users

 

Q: If drill-down is not working in SAC live model, what could be the cause?

A: Possible causes are:

  • Missing primary keys
  • Incorrect relationships
  • Missing hierarchies
  • Incorrect column properties
  • Live model limitations

Solution steps:

  • Verify keys and relationships
  • Configure hierarchies
  • Adjust column properties

Please go to https:://learning.sap.com/live-sessions to search for other live sessions, too.

If you missed this live session, you can also ask your questions regarding this topic here.

entry.title: Working with SAP Business Data Cloud in the SAP Business AI Platform: The Data Engineer Perspective
entry.content:
Assistants and agents are becoming regular consumers of the data products you build. They support decisions and execute multi-step tasks across SAP and third-party systems, and unlike human analysts, they treat what they receive as business truth. A stale metric that a planner might question could be used by an AI agent as fact, turning a data quality issue into a flawed recommendation or automated action. For data engineers, the requirement is clear: data products must be current, complete, semantically correct, and authorized.

SAP Business AI Platform brings together the capabilities needed to build, run, and govern AI, including the business data and context used to ground it. Within this platform, SAP Business Data Cloud (SAP BDC) provides the governed data foundation and shared business semantics, while SAP Knowledge Graph adds relationships and process context. For data engineers, the focus is on keeping this foundation reliable from source to consumption: connecting systems, orchestrating data flows, preserving business context, monitoring freshness and quality, handling change and failure, maintaining traceability, and enabling governed access across platforms.

 

What stays the same

The fundamentals of data engineering remain. You still design, build, and operate pipelines that connect source systems with the environments where data is governed, processed, and consumed across SAP and non-SAP landscapes. The work still involves large data volumes, complex dependencies, transformations, changing schemas, and workloads that must remain dependable as source systems evolve.

You also continue to work closely with data modelers and data stewards. Modelers define structures, relationships, calculations, and business entities. Stewards establish ownership, quality expectations, certification, and governance requirements. Data engineers operationalize those decisions by implementing pipelines, preserving semantics through transformations, enforcing technical controls, and keeping products reliable in production. The core responsibility is unchanged: make trusted business data available where and when it is needed.

SAP BDC strengthens this work with integration, orchestration, governed sharing, semantics, lineage, and monitoring capabilities across SAP and non-SAP landscapes. A business data fabric does not eliminate the need for engineering discipline. It gives pipelines, data products, semantics, lineage, and sharing a common purpose: making business data usable across analytics, planning, applications, and AI without rebuilding context for every consumer.

 

What changes in practice

The first change is the consumer. AI assistants and agents become first-class consumers of data products alongside analysts, applications, planning tools, and data science workloads, and they consume data differently from experienced human users. A planner may recognize that an inventory figure looks stale or know that a status code has an undocumented exception. An agent cannot be expected to have that knowledge. The data product must expose freshness, meaning, relationships, quality, and access explicitly.

The second change is the unit of delivery. Instead of building datasets and pipelines for individual use cases, data engineers increasingly deliver governed, reusable data products. SAP-managed data products provide ready-to-use SAP application data with business context, reducing the need to build and maintain pipelines that extract and reconstruct this data from source systems. This allows data engineers to focus more on creating derived data products - combining, transforming, and enriching SAP and non-SAP data for organization-specific needs.

The third change is operations. AI-ready data engineering moves away from “batch and forget” toward controlled orchestration and continuous visibility into freshness, volume, schema drift, dependencies, failures, and quality thresholds. A successful job execution is not enough. The resulting product must remain discoverable, explainable, governed, observable, and dependable for both people and AI. That means engineering for failure as deliberately as for success: retries, recovery, dependency management, alerts, reconciliation, lineage, and clear signals when a data product can no longer be trusted downstream.

Whatever the consumption pattern, the requirement is the same: reliable AI depends on reliable data products.

 

How AI-ready data engineering works with SAP BDC

Think of AI-ready data engineering as a productized data supply chain. Operational systems provide business facts. Pipelines ingest, replicate, transform, harmonize, and prepare them. Master data and semantic models establish consistent meaning. Catalog and lineage make the resulting products discoverable and traceable. Governed access makes them reusable across platforms. The shift is not only from source to target, but from data movement to governed context, which SAP Business AI Platform can consume so assistants and agents can support decisions and execute approved steps.

Consider supply planning. A change in demand may affect procurement, manufacturing, inventory, and logistics. The engineering challenge is not to copy a demand table from one system to another; it is to assemble and operate a dependable product that provides current context across the process. You might combine SAP-managed product, supplier, inventory, and demand data with logistics signals from a third-party environment through SAP Datasphere and governed zero-copy access, with master data keeping materials, suppliers, customers, and partners consistent. You then make that product operational: orchestrating dependencies, preserving semantics through transformations, monitoring freshness and quality, exposing lineage, enforcing access, and designing recovery for when a source or step fails. The same product can then support a demand-risk model, an AI agent, and a planner in SAP Analytics Cloud without a separate pipeline or separate interpretation for each.

The goal is not to engineer “for AI” as a separate data stack. It is to engineer reusable business data products reliable enough to serve analytics, applications, planning, models, assistants, and agents through the same governed foundation. That foundation is stronger when the architecture is explicit: layers, product types, transformation rules, and reusable blueprints give both human teams and AI-assisted delivery clear guardrails.

This also changes the multi-cloud question. With SAP Business Data Cloud Connect and zero-copy patterns, data does not need to be copied into every environment where processing or AI takes place. The engineering question is no longer only “How do I make this data available?” but also “Does this data need to be copied, or can it be governed and consumed where it already lives?”

 

Impact on trust and operations

In an Autonomous Enterprise, trust depends directly on operations. If an agent recommends a procurement action, triggers a workflow, or supports an exception decision, teams may need to know which data product informed it, where that data originated, how it was transformed, how current it was, whether it passed quality checks, and whether the consumer was authorized to use it. The pipeline is the first link in that accountability chain.

A pipeline can be technically running while its output is operationally unsafe: a source may have stopped updating, a schema change may have altered a transformation, a dependency may have completed with incomplete records, or a replicated table may be available but outside its freshness target. AI-ready engineering means monitoring the state of the data product, not only the state of the job.

Lineage is equally practical. If an AI output references “net revenue by region,” that metric should resolve to the same governed definition used by reporting and analytics, not to an undocumented parallel calculation. Teams need to trace the path from source through transformation to the product consumed downstream and identify where a problem entered it. The same applies to recovery: when something fails, the design should make it possible to identify affected products and consumers, restore processing safely, reconcile the data, and determine when the product can again be treated as trustworthy.

Side channels, ad hoc scripts, and unregistered staging areas make all of this harder. If a data flow is invisible to catalog, lineage, monitoring, and governance, it becomes harder to establish whether an AI agent should depend on it. For AI-ready data products, operational reliability and trust are two sides of the same engineering problem.

 

How this maps to SAP BDC components

SAP BDC brings together capabilities that address different parts of the data engineering lifecycle, with SAP-managed data products as the starting point.

  • SAP-managed data products provide governed SAP application data with business semantics already preserved, reducing the need for data engineers to build and maintain pipelines that extract and reconstruct the same data from source systems. Engineers can consume these products directly or use them as the foundation for derived data products that combine, transform, and enrich SAP and non-SAP data.
  • SAP Datasphere supports integration, modeling, and sharing across the business data fabric. Data engineers can connect SAP and non-SAP data, create derived data products, and use catalog and lineage capabilities to make them discoverable and traceable.
  • SAP BW allows existing BW data and business logic to participate in SAP BDC as data products while retaining established business meaning, reducing the need to reconstruct proven logic in new pipelines.
  • SAP HANA Cloud supports real-time processing, transformations, calculation views, application-facing data, and retrieval patterns such as vector search.
  • SAP Databricks and SAP Snowflake extend SAP BDC with governed data engineering, analytics, data warehousing, and AI/ML capabilities across data lakehouse and warehouse architectures.
  • SAP Master Data Governance and SAP Reltio support consistent master data across SAP and non-SAP landscapes, so data products and pipelines operate on harmonized business entities.
  • SAP Business Data Cloud Connect enables governed sharing and zero-copy access to data products across SAP Databricks, SAP Snowflake, and supported third-party platforms, allowing data to be used where processing occurs without unnecessary replication.
  • SAP Knowledge Graph connects governed data products and their business semantics through relationships and process context, providing richer context for AI reasoning.
  • SAP Business AI Platform uses this governed data and business context to build, run, and govern AI applications and agents.
  • Joule Studio supports custom agents and skills and will become the home of the data product creation agent, bringing AI-assisted data product development into the engineering workflow.
  • SAP Integration Suite connects agents to approved APIs, events, and workflows when AI reasoning needs to translate into actions across systems.

The value is not that every workload moves into one technology. SAP-managed data products provide a governed starting point, so data engineers do not have to rebuild pipelines and business context that SAP already provides. They can focus instead on integrating additional data, creating derived data products, and operating those products reliably across platforms. This requires clear responsibility for ingestion, transformation, semantics, orchestration, sharing, monitoring, lineage, and consumption across the architecture.

 

Where data engineers should focus next

Preparing for AI does not require data engineers to learn an entirely new discipline. It requires applying familiar engineering practices to governed data products that may now be consumed by analysts, applications, assistants, and agents.

  • Build on governed data products and minimize data replication. Reuse SAP-managed or organization-specific data products when they already expose the required business data, semantics, and governance. Create derived data products only when additional transformation, enrichment, or reusable logic is needed. Prefer zero-copy access, federation, and virtualized consumption where technically appropriate, and introduce physical replication only when required for performance, resilience, or workload isolation.
  • Engineer for data reliability, not just pipeline success. Define measurable expectations for freshness, completeness, accuracy, and availability, and monitor them at the data-product level. Design explicitly for source outages, schema evolution, dependency failures, late or missing data, reconciliation, replay, and recovery. A successful pipeline run does not guarantee that the resulting data product is current, complete, correct, or ready for consumption.
  • Preserve business semantics and end-to-end traceability. When transforming, enriching, or combining data, retain the business meaning required to interpret it, including calculation logic, units, currencies, relationships, keys, and hierarchies. Use the lineage capabilities available in SAP BDC to trace data from source through transformation to downstream products and consumers. Where end-to-end lineage cannot be captured automatically, document the missing lineage so that dependencies and traceability gaps are clear.
  • Control how data is consumed by AI. Assistants and agents should access data through the same authorization, governance, and policy controls as other consumers. Expose sufficient metadata and operational signals for AI consumers to determine whether a data product is fresh, complete, reliable, and appropriate for the intended use. AI systems should not treat a data product as current business truth when its operational state cannot be established.

Above all, engineer and operate for the state of the data product, not merely the state of the pipeline. Pipeline execution is an implementation detail. What matters to consumers is whether the resulting data is trustworthy and fit for use. For AI workloads in particular, freshness, quality, lineage, and operational reliability are integral to trustworthy business context.

 

The takeaway

SAP Business AI Platform does not replace data engineering with AI. It increases the importance of good data engineering. Pipelines no longer support only reports, dashboards, and applications. They shape what assistants and agents know, how current that knowledge is, which business meaning applies, and whether an AI-supported action can be traced back to governed and authorized data.

SAP BDC provides the governed data foundation, managed data products, and platform capabilities. Data engineers make that foundation operational by integrating additional sources, creating derived data products, orchestrating data flows, handling scale and change, monitoring freshness and quality, maintaining traceability, engineering recovery, and making governed data products dependable enough to be reused across analytics and AI. In the Autonomous Enterprise, that reliability is part of what makes AI-supported execution possible.

What are you seeing in your own SAP BDC projects? Are your pipelines and data products ready to support AI assistants and agents, or are freshness, observability, lineage, and recovery still evolving? Join the Data Professionals community to discuss engineering patterns and share how you are using SAP BDC as a foundation for the Autonomous Enterprise.

 

How data engineers fit into the BDC data team

This blog is part of a series that explores how the SAP Business AI Platform (BAIP) impacts day‑to‑day work across key data professional roles.

Each role in this series contributes a different part of the trusted business context that analytics, applications, assistants, and agents need. The relationship between the data engineer, data modeler, and data steward is particularly close: modelers define the semantic structures that give a product meaning, stewards establish ownership, certification, and quality expectations, and data engineers turn those definitions into running systems through ingestion, transformation, orchestration, monitoring, lineage, access, and recovery. Data analysts validate and consume insights, data scientists develop and evaluate models, AI engineers build retrieval patterns and agents, and enterprise architects set landscape guardrails. The data engineer is the operational backbone, turning governed business context into reliable, current, scalable, resilient, and production-ready data products.

entry.title: Releasing SAC Pilot: The Ultimate Productivity Browser Extension for SAP Analytics Cloud
entry.content:
If you build stories, write analytical scripts, configure planning simulations, or manage models inside SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), you know the daily friction all too well:

  • You are deep in the middle of designing a critical dashboard or calculation, and you need to look up a specific Cost Center code, Hierarchy parent node, or Dimension Member ID.
  • You have to navigate completely away from your active story canvas or launch an entirely separate browser tab.
  • The SAC Modeler takes 30 to 60 seconds to boot up its heavy menus, breaking your concentration and flow.
  • You only wanted a quick master data export or a clean CSV extract of fact data, but you were forced to step through a multi-step export wizard.
  • Transporting stories between Development, QA, and Production environments often breaks unexpectedly because a single dimension member was missing or had different attributes across tenants.

We built SAC Pilot to eliminate this friction once and for all. It is an independent, 100% client-side browser extension that sits pinned right inside your browser's native side panel, auto-detects your active SAP Analytics Cloud session, and helps you work faster without ever leaving your canvas.

What is SAC Pilot?

SAC Pilot is an open-community, high-performance browser extension crafted specifically for SAC Story Designers, Planners, BI Consultants, and Enterprise Architects. It operates directly alongside your active SAP Analytics Cloud workspace across Google Chrome (recommended), Microsoft Edge, Brave, Opera, and Mozilla Firefox.

Unlike traditional add-ons or middleware that require server installations, database connections, or complicated OAuth setup, SAC Pilot uses a Zero-Configuration, Zero-Trust architecture. It securely senses your existing, authenticated browser session cookie and directly queries the tenant's REST and OData APIs over HTTPS.

Key Features & Capabilities

SAC Pilot packs over 15+ specialized power tools and utilities into a single, cohesive side-panel interface:

1. Instant Model & Data Provider Browser

Features type-ahead autocomplete search across all Analytical Models, Planning Models, and Data Providers configured within your tenant. You can view technical model IDs, descriptions, and data source metadata instantly, and switch between models in a single click without page reloads.

2. Dimension Member & Hierarchy Tree Explorer

Look up dimension member IDs, descriptions, and custom property attributes in sub-seconds. Explore complex parent-child hierarchy trees with interactive rollup expansion, allowing you to trace drill-down levels and aggregation paths on the fly.

3. High-Throughput Fact Data Exporter

Stream millions of transactional fact records directly from SAC models at blazing speeds (up to 100,000+ records per second) with live throughput progress indicators and time-remaining estimates. Download pristine CSV or JSON extracts ready for Microsoft Excel, Python, or data pipelines.

4. Reverse CSV Fact Data Importer

Upload external CSV datasets directly back into your SAC planning models without opening backend data integration wizards. The tool maps columns, validates schemas, and pushes records directly into the model.

5. Visual Column & Measure Filter Builder

Construct complex OData query filters visually before downloading data. Filter by dimension members, posting periods, version tags, or numerical measure ranges to retrieve only the exact dataset slice you need.

6. Planning Version Manager (Edit, Copy & Publish)

Inspect both Public and Private planning versions at a glance. Review version publication states, ownership, and creation timestamps. Trigger one-click data publishing, create version copies, and manage planning simulations effortlessly.

7. User & Team Inspector (SCIM Governance)

Audit and search tenant users, email directories, assigned roles, and security teams without needing full SAC Administration menu access. Perfect for validating permissions and verifying user provisioning.

8. Currency Exchange Rate Inspector

Instantly inspect Currency Conversion Tables configured on your tenant. Review exchange rate types, source and target currency pairs, and effective date validity ranges without opening Modeler settings.

9. Multi-Tenant Comparator (Dev vs. QA vs. Prod)

Compare dimension structures and member records between two different SAC tenant environments. The diff engine flags synced members, attribute differences, and missing members in the target tenant, helping you catch missing master data before transporting stories.

10. Synthetic Mock Test Data Generator

Automatically generate structured, realistic mock transactional fact data matching your model's exact dimension schemas. Configure cardinality, random distributions, and date ranges to stage models for testing and demonstration.

11. In-Panel Visualizer & Analytics

Embedded Chart.js analytics right inside the extension panel. Render instant bar charts, measure distribution curves, and member cardinality breakdowns without needing to create disposable story widgets.

12. Smart Bookmarks & Saved Filter Queries

Bookmark your most frequently accessed models, dimensions, and custom filter configurations. Jump straight into your daily operational views with one click.

13. 1-Click Clipboard Utilities

Copy individual member IDs, formatted string arrays, or JSON arrays directly to your system clipboard, formatted specifically for pasting into SAC story calculation scripts, advanced formulas, or SQL queries.

14. Public Dimensions Explorer

Dedicated inspection view for tenant-wide shared Public Dimensions, allowing you to audit global master data independent of individual analytical models.

15. Application Audit Logs Explorer

Inspect model application audit logs and change histories directly within the extension to audit updates and track modifications.

16. Deep Link Story & Modeler Navigator

Generate one-click direct deep links to navigate straight to the exact model or story in the native SAC interface.

Feature Overview Table

 

 

Feature CategoryTool NamePrimary BenefitsTarget User
Data ExportHigh-Throughput Fact ExporterStream fact data at 100k+ rows/sec to CSV/JSONBI Analysts & Data Engineers
Data ImportReverse CSV ImporterPush external fact datasets into modelsPlanners & Data Modelers
Master DataDimension & Hierarchy ExplorerInstant member search & parent-child tree drill-downStory Designers & Planners
PlanningVersion ManagerReview, copy, and publish planning versions in 1 clickFinancial Planners
GovernanceUser & Team InspectorSCIM audit of users, roles, and teamsAdministrators & Leads
Quality AssuranceTenant ComparatorDiff dimensions across Dev, QA, and ProdRelease Managers & Architects
TestingTest Data GeneratorGenerate synthetic mock facts based on model schemaModel Developers & Testers
FinanceCurrency Table InspectorAudit conversion rates and currency pairsFinancial Controllers
ProductivitySmart Bookmarks & ClipboardSave frequent queries and copy arrays for scriptingAll SAC Users
SecurityAES-256 GCM Storage VaultZero-trust, client-side encryption of all local cachesSecurity & Compliance Teams

Zero-Trust Architecture & Enterprise Security

Enterprise data privacy is non-negotiable. SAC Pilot was designed from the ground up to comply with strict enterprise IT security standards:

  1. 100% Client-Side Operation: The extension operates entirely within your local browser. There are no intermediate proxy servers, cloud relays, or backend databases.
  2. Direct HTTPS Communication: Every network call is dispatched directly between your browser and your authenticated SAC tenant domain.
  3. No Telemetry or Tracking: SAC Pilot collects zero personal information, logs no tenant activity, and includes no third-party tracking scripts.
  4. AES-256 GCM Encrypted Vault: Any data persisted locally (such as bookmarks and cached dimension names) is encrypted using the browser's native Web Crypto API before being written to storage.
  5. Session Cookie Inheritance: SAC Pilot never asks for, stores, or handles your password. It relies entirely on your browser's existing authenticated SAC session cookie.
  6. Instant Data Purge: A dedicated single-click "Wipe Storage" option in the Settings panel allows you to instantly purge all stored keys, bookmarks, and local data.

How to Install & Get Started

You can install SAC Pilot directly from the official portal:

Official Installation Website: sac-pilot.rohitchouhan.com

Easy 3-Step Installation:

  1. Go to sac-pilot.rohitchouhan.com in your browser.
  2. Click the install button for your browser (Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, Opera, or Mozilla Firefox).
  3. Confirm the prompt to add the extension to your browser.

Getting Started in 60 Seconds:

  1. Log in to your regular SAP Analytics Cloud tenant.
  2. Open SAC Pilot by clicking the extension icon in your browser toolbar or opening your browser's native Side Panel.
  3. The extension automatically detects your active authenticated SAC session — no API keys, logins, or configurations needed.
  4. Select any tool from the Home screen (such as Data Export/Import, Dimension Explorer, or Version Manager) and start exploring your data right beside your active stories.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Does SAC Pilot require an API key, Login Credentials or SAC OAuth client setup?
No. SAC Pilot automatically uses your existing authenticated browser session cookies to interact with SAC's standard endpoints. No administrator API configuration is required.

Can SAC Pilot see or transmit my company's data?
Never. SAC Pilot runs 100% inside your client browser. It never connects to any external third-party server. All data stays strictly between your browser and your company's official SAC tenant.

Does it support both Classic and New Planning Models?
Yes. SAC Pilot supports Analytical Models, Classic Account Models, and the New Model (Measure-based) type.

Is SAC Pilot free to use?
Yes, SAC Pilot is an open-community tool designed to give back to the SAP Analytics Cloud ecosystem.

All other company, product, and service names used are for identification purposes only and belong to their respective owners.
  • Independent Companion Tool: This tool is created independently as an open-community utility for SAP Analytics Cloud practitioners to improve productivity.
  • No Official Affiliation: Reference to SAP Analytics Cloud does not imply any affiliation with or endorsement by SAP SE. The official SAP website is located at https://www.sap.com.
  • Warranty & Compliance: This software is provided on an "as-is" basis without warranties of any kind. Users are responsible for adhering to their organization's internal data governance and security policies when handling corporate tenant data.

Conclusion

SAC Pilot transforms the way professionals interact with SAP Analytics Cloud by removing friction, accelerating daily tasks, and providing deep data visibility right beside your active work. Whether you are validating a single dimension member, streaming a million fact records, or diffing master data across enterprise environments, SAC Pilot is your trusted companion.

entry.title: SAP TechEd 2026: Must-Attend Sessions for Data Professionals
entry.content:
SAP TechEd 2026 (October 27–29) offers no shortage of sessions on data, AI, architecture, and analytics. The harder question is which ones deserve a place on your agenda. With SAP Business Data Cloud now in production and AI capabilities expanding across the SAP portfolio, this year’s most valuable sessions should help you, the practitioner, move beyond product updates to make better decisions about what to build, govern, modernize, and scale.

This blog narrows the field to the sessions I believe are most relevant for five data and AI practitioner personas: Enterprise Architects, Data Stewards, Data Engineers, Data Analysts, and Data Scientists. The selections emphasize practical takeaways, from designing governed data foundations and modernizing pipelines to enabling trusted, context-rich AI, so you can focus on the sessions most likely to inform your next project.

Whether attending in-person or virtual start building your agenda now — choose the sessions that match your role and share your must-attend picks with peers in the Data and AI Professionals community to keep the conversation and practical learning going well beyond the event.

This list reflects my own picks, so I've likely missed a few gems. If there's a session you're planning to attend that didn't make the cut, drop it in the comments — I'd love to know what's on your radar.

 

Keynotes

KEY100 | Built for the ones who build

KEY100V | Built for the ones who build (virtual)

Why Attend

SAP TechEd's opening keynote answers the question every architect and practitioner is asking: what can I actually build on SAP's AI platform today? SAP unifies AI, business data, governance, agents, and a new UX layer into one integrated platform — eliminating manual data pipelines, model training overhead, and unpredictable AI costs. Hear directly from SAP leadership what is production-ready now and leave with a clear picture of the business outcomes you can start delivering immediately.

Key Takeaways

  • SAP Business AI Platform unifies AI, data, governance, agents, and UX into one platform — eliminating manual pipeline setup, training overhead, and unpredictable infrastructure costs.
  • Designed so developers, architects, and practitioners focus on building outcomes, not managing underlying complexity.
  • For IT leaders evaluating adoption timelines, this session defines what is production-ready now versus what is on the horizon.

 

KEY101 | Agent v0.0.7 - A license to skill

KEY101V | Agent v0.0.7 - A license to skill (virtual)

Why Attend

Master the AI-driven development revolution. Join Agent Kasimir to see how SAP Business AI Platform, Joule Studio, and open ecosystem tools empower practitioners in AI-driven development. The session shows data professionals how agentic orchestration and context-aware AI work together — redefining how enterprise solutions are built across SAP and non-SAP environments. Evaluating how AI agents fit your analytics workflows? This session moves you from concept to action.

Key Takeaways

  • Joule Studio gives practitioners a supported entry point to build and orchestrate enterprise-grounded AI agents — without starting from scratch.
  • Data professionals get a path to AI workflows where agents reason over business data, coordinate, and integrate across SAP and non-SAP tools.
  • SAP's agentic AI is built on openness — ecosystem tools sit first-class alongside SAP-native capabilities, amplifying existing investments, not displacing them.

 

Enterprise Architects

ST135 | Agent interoperability: Protocols, patterns, and enterprise strategy

Why Attend

As multi-agent AI reaches enterprise scale, interoperability becomes an architectural imperative — this strategy session delivers the protocol-level knowledge architects and developers need. It covers open standards and integration patterns, including A2A and MCP, enabling secure, composable agent networks across SAP and third-party platforms. Leave with the foundation for enterprise-scale AI architectures designed to interoperate — not just orchestrate.

Key Takeaways

  • Agent2Agent (A2A) defines how AI agents from different vendors communicate — the foundational protocol for multi-agent networks spanning SAP and third-party systems.
  • MCP governs agent access to enterprise tools and APIs — mastering A2A and MCP together is essential for reliable cross-platform architectures at enterprise scale.
  • The session delivers practical patterns for building secure, composable agent networks across SAP and non-SAP — a blueprint for expanding agent ecosystems confidently.

 

XP113 | Build AI agents on SAP and non-SAP data and context in an open lakehouse

Why Attend

If your organization is evaluating SAP Business Data Cloud with Dremio, this is the technical blueprint for building AI agents that reason across your full data estate without siloed or ungoverned copies. The session shows how architects and developers use Apache Iceberg and Apache Polaris to integrate SAP and third-party data in an open lakehouse — creating governed data products and ontologies that power Joule agents and enable external consumption through A2A. You'll leave with a clear, end-to-end path from unified data to production-ready agentic AI.

Key Takeaways

  • An open lakehouse on Apache Iceberg and Apache Polaris unifies SAP and third-party data into a single governed layer — giving AI agents real-time access to the full data estate without movement, duplication, or governance compromise.
  • Zero-copy access ensures AI agents always reason over current, authoritative data — reducing management overhead while keeping security and compliance controls intact.
  • A2A protocols extend governed data products beyond SAP boundaries — giving architects a composable foundation where Joule and third-party agents access business context through standardized, controlled interfaces.

 

RA110 | Joule and SAP Knowledge Graph: Context-aware AI across SAP solutions

RA110V | Joule and SAP Knowledge Graph: Context-aware AI across SAP solutions (virtual)

Why Attend

Context separates a generically intelligent AI from one that truly understands your business — this session reveals how SAP AI Core, the orchestration layer behind Joule, delivers that context at scale. You’ll learn how to extend Joule Agents, leverage the Joule Studio model library, connect SAP Business Data Cloud data products, and embed AI directly in SAP S/4HANA. For professionals designing AI agent architectures or SAP analytics integrations, this is where governance, context, and intelligence converge in a production-ready architecture.

Key Takeaways

  • SAP AI Core is the orchestration layer that governs how Joule agents access models, coordinate reasoning, and embed AI directly into SAP S/4HANA within a fully auditable architecture.
  • Joule agents ground every action in trusted data via SAP Business Data Cloud and AI Core, while SAP Knowledge Graph anchors reasoning in real business relationships — delivering business-aware decisions, not generic predictions.
  • The result is an AI architecture where context, governance, and intelligence are built in by design — giving architects a production-ready foundation for extending Joule across analytics, planning, and S/4HANA use cases.

 

Data Stewards

ST200 | The next evolution of SAP Business Data Cloud with Dremio and SAP Reltio

Why Attend

SAP’s 2026 acquisitions of Dremio and Reltio are reshaping Business Data Cloud’s data fabric — this session gives architects and stewards the full picture on governance, master data quality, and the trusted foundation agentic AI requires — and what your organization needs to act on now.

Key Takeaways

  • Dremio’s Iceberg-native integration extends Business Data Cloud into an enterprise lakehouse — giving AI agents zero-copy access to current, authoritative SAP and non-SAP data while preserving governance.
  • SAP Reltio delivers AI-native MDM to Business Data Cloud — harmonizing trusted golden records across data domains so agents have the consistent reference layer they need to reason reliably in production.
  • Together, Dremio and Reltio close enterprise AI’s two critical gaps — unified data access without duplication, and trusted master data quality — delivering the governed foundation agentic AI demands at scale.

 

XP826 | Get a road map to your data products foundation: Powering AI outcomes

Why Attend

AI agents deliver value only when they know what data exists, where it lives, and whether it can be trusted. This session gives architects and stewards a practical road map for integrating governance, quality, and context to make enterprise data AI-ready — so agents can query the right information at scale to drive measurable outcomes.

Key Takeaways

  • Trusted data foundations require ongoing discipline — governance, quality, and semantic context at every layer so agents can discover, assess, and act with confidence.
  • Governance, quality, and context must travel with the data — keeping agents within defined trust boundaries wherever data resides.
  • Data products — governed, reusable, context-enriched units — are the building block for scaling AI outcomes, letting multiple agents consume trusted data without duplicating governance effort.

 

DA104 | Reimagining master data as the foundation for enterprise AI

Why Attend

AI agents grounded in inconsistent or ungoverned master data produce unreliable outcomes — this session reframes MDM as the strategic prerequisite for trusted AI at scale. See how SAP Business Data Cloud unifies, governs, and delivers master data as reusable products that ground analytics, autonomous applications, and AI agents in consistent, trustworthy business context.

Key Takeaways

  • Structured master data products keep agents grounded in consistent, authoritative context — eliminating the inconsistency that causes unreliable or contradictory outputs in production.
  • Data stewards now hold a critical AI risk role — the governance rules, quality thresholds, and semantic metadata they define directly determine agent accuracy and auditability.
  • Master data quality is a strategic AI enabler, not just an operational concern — organizations investing in governed master data through SAP Business Data Cloud will deploy reliable, scalable agentic AI ahead of those that do not.

 

Data Engineers

DA100 | Enhancing agentic AI with trusted business data 

DA100V | Enhancing agentic AI with trusted business data (virtual)

Why Attend

This session answers a critical enterprise AI question: how do you ensure agents access accurate, governed, and contextually rich business data? Learn how SAP Business Data Cloud’s zero-copy architecture enables AI agents to consume trusted enterprise data in place — reducing data movement while maintaining the security, compliance, and control production AI demands.

Key Takeaways

  • Zero-copy architecture gives AI agents in-place access to enterprise data — eliminating movement and duplication while keeping governance controls fully intact.
  • Data product-level governance ensures context, permissions, and semantic meaning travel with the data — making agent outputs trustworthy and auditable by design, not retrospective monitoring.
  • Together, zero-copy access and data product-level governance shift AI quality assurance from reactive to proactive — giving architects a scalable, compliance-ready foundation for deploying agents with confidence.

 

DA200 | Agentic SAP BW modernization: Your path to SAP Business Data Cloud

Why Attend

If your organization is still running SAP BW and evaluating modernization, this session delivers the most current practical guidance available — including how AI agents now accelerate the migration journey. Explore proven strategies and dedicated tools that simplify the move to SAP Business Data Cloud while maximizing the value of your existing BW investments.

Key Takeaways

  • Dedicated migration tools and AI agents now automate large portions of the SAP BW modernization journey — reducing manual effort and resource demands while maximizing existing investments.
  • Modernizing to SAP Business Data Cloud isn’t starting over — existing BW models, hierarchies, and business logic are repositioned in a governed, AI-ready data fabric as the foundation for agentic AI, analytics, and planning.
  • Moving to SAP Business Data Cloud is both a technical migration and a strategic upgrade — organizations that modernize now gain a governed, purpose-built agentic AI platform ahead of those still constrained by legacy BW.

 

CT1163 | Under the hood of the Delta Sharing protocol

Why Attend

Zero-copy data sharing is the architectural standard for AI-ready data ecosystems — this technical session gives data engineers the depth to understand and implement the open-source Delta Sharing protocol across cloud and hybrid environments. See how a Delta Sharing server delivers live Delta tables from S3-compatible storage directly to consumers like Databricks — no data movement, no duplication, and governance built in.

Key Takeaways

  • Delta Sharing delivers a zero-copy architecture — live Delta tables stream from S3-compatible storage directly to cloud consumers like Databricks with no duplication, governance and access controls intact.
  • A Delta Sharing server gives engineers practical knowledge to ingest, govern, and operationalize live data sharing between hybrid storage and cloud-native analytics and AI platforms.
  • Together, zero-copy sharing and open standards eliminate two persistent barriers — data movement and proprietary lock-in — giving engineers a replicable, vendor-neutral pattern for connecting distributed data to AI and analytics workloads at scale.

 

Data Analysts

DA105 | Enriching AI models with SAP AI Core in SAP Business Data Cloud

Why Attend

AI models are only as powerful as their business context — this deep dive shows data scientists and practitioners how SAP AI Core integrates with SAP Business Data Cloud to enable semantically enriched, enterprise-grade AI. Learn how to enhance models with rich data products from SAP Business Data Cloud, supporting benchmarking, custom AI development, agentic analytics, and production-ready applications.

Key Takeaways

  • SAP Business Data Cloud data products enrich AI models with business-specific terminology, entity relationships, and domain context — delivering accurate, enterprise-relevant outputs without the overhead of extensive custom training.
  • The session delivers a practical, end-to-end path from governed data to production AI — a clear, repeatable technical approach for agentic analytics practitioners can apply immediately.
  • SAP Business Data Cloud and SAP AI Core carry semantic richness and governance from data products directly into AI model development — closing the gap between trusted enterprise data and reliable, auditable AI outcomes at scale.

 

DA260 | Accelerate agentic planning with trusted data products (hands-on workshop)

Why Attend

The most practical TechEd 2026 session for SAP planning professionals — a 2-hour workshop where you actually build agentic planning workflows, not just hear about them. Work directly with governed data products in SAP Business Data Cloud and SAP Analytics Cloud, learning how agentic AI automates planning tasks, generates insights, and drives faster, more informed decisions.
